tagline: Up a red rock canyon to an old volcano's floor.
intro: From US 550 at San Ysidro, NM 4 runs north past Jemez Pueblo and up the red rock of San Diego Canyon beside the Jemez River, under high volcanic cliffs, to the village of Jemez Springs. Then it climbs steeply into the Santa Fe National Forest, skirts the Valles Caldera and drops on hairpin turns toward Los Alamos. A second arm, NM 126, goes west by Fenton Lake to Cuba, and US 550 brings the loop back south.
Jemez Springs had its bathhouse by the 1880s. In 1942 it was the second choice for the Manhattan Project laboratory. Los Alamos, up the road, got it.

moments.title: Jemez Historic Site
moments.text: North of the village stand the limestone walls of San José de los Jémez, a mission church 110 feet long, begun in 1621 beside the older Gíusewa Pueblo. The pueblo emptied in 1680.

moments.title: Valles Caldera
moments.text: A volcanic caldera nearly 14 miles across, with grass valleys below Redondo Peak. Valle Grande, the largest of them, is the only one a paved road reaches.

moments.title: Cabezon Peak
moments.text: Cabezon means big head. The volcanic plug stands nearly 2,000 feet over the Rio Puerco valley, and in Navajo tradition it is the head of a giant the twins slew.
